en: The *Vajrabhairava-saṃgraha-vipula-vidhi-avalokiteśvara-bodhisattva-trikāla-parama-hṛdaya-mantra-rāja-sūtra*.
Translated by [the monk] holding the rank of Kai-fu-yi-tong-san-si,
Te-jin, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, and Duke of Su.

The Monk Amoghavajra, a Tripitaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, who was granted a fief of three thousand households, invested with the purple robe, promoted to the rank of Minister of Works, and posthumously honored with the title "Great Mirror" (Dajian) and the epithet "Great Universal Wisdom" (Dayangzhi), translated this by imperial decree. Chapter One: The Introduction Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Buddha was dwelling within a palace on the variegated peaks of the Great Mountain Jewel-Crest,
a place adorned with hundreds of thousands of jeweled canopies and various rows of trees,
strewn and beautified with delightful fragrant flowers.
He was surrounded by a retinue of one thousand two hundred and fifty great arhats, including Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Śāriputra, Ānanda, and others;
he was also accompanied by immeasurable bodhisattvas, headed by Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Ratnaketu Bodhisattva, and others.
Furthermore, there were Vaiśravaṇa,
Pūrṇabhadra, and Pañcika.
Brahmā, Śakra, Nārāyaṇa, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and bhūtas.
Piśācas, kiṃnaras,
mahoragas, and hundreds of thousands of such attendants stood surrounding him,
paying homage and making offerings with reverence.

At that time, the Tathāgata sat upon a great lion throne variegated with various jewels and expounded for the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and others the essential Dharma teachings on the practices of the bodhisattvas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One,
circumambulated the Buddha three times, bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, and joined his palms in reverent salutation.
Then he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, by means of one dharma, I have given rise to love, delight, and joy.
With a mind of great compassion and diligent vigor, I bring about benefit and happiness, providing protection for sentient beings."
This is the King of the Vidyārājas of one's own mind,
named "Supreme among the Three Times.
I now desire to expound this Dharma.
The Buddha said, "Mahāsattva, speak it now. Then,
receiving the Buddha’s instruction, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara immediately spoke the mantra of his own heart, saying:

Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya. Bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya. Tadyathā: padma-padma-padmini. Sara sara. E he he. Vagvan. Aryāvalokiteśvara aruḥ. Furthermore, the mantra of the head is spoken as follows:
Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo 'ryāvalokiteśvarāya. Oṃ āḥ. This is the mantra of the crown.
The mantra for the eye, *Oṃ āḥ hūṃ*, is as follows:
The heart mantra, *Oṃ āḥ jvala*, is as follows:
The armor mantra, *Oṃ āḥ phaṭ*, is as follows:
The mantra for *Oṃ āḥ pāda-khaḍga* is: Oṃ āḥ tvara-sphara.
The mantra for *Oṃ āḥ viśvara-jvāla* is: Oṃ āḥ viśvara-jvāla.
The mantra for *Oṃ āḥ viśvara-śara* is: Oṃ āḥ viśvara-śara.
The mantra of Oṃ Aḥ Hana is: Oṃ Aḥ Naha Cāṅ. The mantra of Oṃ Aḥ Naha Cāṅ is:
Oṃ Aḥ Nara Kṣa. The supreme heart-mantra is: Oṃ Aḥ Nara Kṣa.
Oṃ āḥ hrīḥ nāthodita. The mantra for awakening the heart is:
Oṃ āḥ hrīḥ nātha. The mantra for generating the heart is: Tannāma.
Oṃ āḥ hṛīḥ nāyūnapa va jvala. The mantra for entering the wheel is:
Oṃ āḥ prasepara. As soon as the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this Great Heart Mantra, which is supreme throughout the three times, etc.
The trichiliocosm shook in six ways,
and the devas rained down exquisite flowers from the sky.
All the cold-water hells—
All attained warmth and comfort;
even the various hot hells, including the Avīci Hell, all became cool.
The radiance shone forth, reaching upward as far as the Akaniṣṭha Heaven.
In the sky, hundreds of thousands of musical instruments resounded spontaneously without being struck.
Devas, nāgas, yakṣas, kinnaras,
and others all offered praise to the Tathāgata and the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
The various māras, obstacles, and vināyakas trembled and wailed aloud.
All the devas, with one voice, praised him in verse, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, O Great Compassionate One! Excellent, O benefactor who uproots suffering!"
"Excellent, excellent, Great Sattva! Excellent, you who accomplish all purposes!
Then, having spoken this vidyārāja, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, this heart-mantra..."
It can pacify all ailments, accomplish all meaningful benefits,
subdue, increase, bring profit and happiness, and establish one in the signless samādhi.
It enables one to practice the meaning of emptiness and opens up hidden treasures;
it can eliminate all poisons of sorcery, spiders, snakes, scorpions, and the like,
and causes all sentient beings to hold one in respectful remembrance.
It can cause those who have already died to return to life;
it can protect against the perils of lions, tigers, wolves, bears, brown bears, and bandits;
and it can destroy malevolent rites, curses, and incantations.
One is able to accomplish the wish-fulfilling jewel and the auspicious vase;
the rain of jewels, the wheel, and the sword;
and the divine thread and the lotus garland.
The ritual water vessel and the rosary can exhaust the great oceans and rivers,
and can accomplish all the food and drink of the devas.
It can manifest the palaces of all the devas for them to enjoy at will;
it can cause Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, to tremble;
and it can summon all trees.
"However, whatever the mind desires to do shall be accomplished.
All the dharmas that I have already taught, as well as those not yet taught, during the *ratnamālā-ratnaketu-maitreya-kalpa* of the past, can all be brought to fulfillment."
Chapter Two: The Chapter on the Accomplishment of Deeds. At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, if there be any sons or daughters of good family..."
If one maintains or recites this heart-mantra,
even without applying further effort, one will be protected from all fears.
No illnesses shall ever afflict their bodies;
whatever words of admonition they utter shall cause others to believe and accept them,
and they shall inspire all sentient beings with reverence and mindfulness.
All devas, ghosts, spirits, yakṣas, rākṣasas, pūtanas, piśācas, gandharvas, mahoragas, and so forth, will not dare to invade or harm them;
they shall never suffer untimely death or premature demise.
One shall not fall into any of the evil realms.
At all times, one's granaries and treasuries shall be overflowing.
One shall attain great *dhāraṇī*, which can eliminate all illnesses.
After the end of this life,
one shall be reborn in a buddha-field where the marks and signs of physical perfection are fully accomplished.
This is the Dharma-gate of Avalokiteśvara Hayagrīva that I have previously taught.
All are accomplished by means of this mantra.
World-Honored One, if a practitioner wishes to attain siddhi,
they must first purify their own aggregates with the five purities.
Having consecrated the site for painting and decoration,
one should receive the rules for the mantras from the mouth of the master;
meanwhile, facing the image of the Buddha, one should subsist solely on milk.
One should make offerings of incense, flowers, lamps, garlands, food, and drink,
reciting the mantra limitlessly for up to seven days.
Following this, one should paint the deity.
It shall be one cubit in circumference and free from all hair;
the painter should observe the eight precepts,
and the pigments should be prepared in new vessels without using animal glue.
In the center is depicted Amitābha Tathāgata,
seated upon a white lotus flower,
his right hand resting in the mudrā of granting boons (varada-mudrā).
To the right is depicted the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
His body is white in color, and he wears a skirt of tiger skin.
He has a waistband made of white crystal jewels and is draped with a black deerskin fastened across his shoulder by its antlers.
She dwells upon a white lotus flower;
her left hand holds a white lotus, and her right hand performs the gesture of granting boons (*varada-mudrā*).
She is without necklaces, bracelets, or armlets.
On the left is painted the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
his body white with a reddish tint, adorned with various precious necklaces and ornaments;
he holds a white fly-whisk in his hand, making the gesture of whisking away [defilements] from the Tathāgata.
The Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and others all gaze upon the practitioner.
The practitioner draws himself beneath the Buddha,
kneeling with his right knee on the ground and holding an incense burner in his hand.
Having gazed upon the noble one,
once the image has been completed,
if a lay practitioner observes the eight precepts;
One should bathe three times a day and change clothes three times a day,
wearing clean white garments.
One should begin this practice from the first day of the month.
Offer white flowers to the Buddha image.
Before the image, fashion one thousand stūpas out of fragrant clay.
Then, perform the preliminary rite of accomplishment before these stūpas.
If one recites it one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*),
all the devas— the Brahmā kings, Maheśvara, Nārāyaṇa, Kumāra, the Seven Mother Goddesses (*saptamātṛkā*), the Garuḍas, and so forth— will all leap for joy.
Then one shall enter the samaya of all maṇḍalas;
all mantras will be accomplished.
Recite [the mantra] two lakṣas.
Vaiśravaṇa and all the yakṣas will be greatly delighted.
By reciting three hundred thousand times,
all mantras within the Vajra family will be accomplished.
If one recites four hundred thousand times,
the mantras of all Tathāgata families will be accomplished.
The practitioner must first perform the preliminary service according to the ritual.
For the first, one should recite one hundred thousand times;
for the second, one should recite two hundred thousand times in the mountains;
and for the third, one should recite three hundred thousand times on the banks of a river.
Fourth, after reciting four hundred thousand [times] before a stūpa,
one should immediately receive the eight precepts and perform limitless recitations before an image for three days.
Thereafter, one shall not eat for three days and three nights.
One should arrange a vast and extensive offering and take lotus flowers, dipping them in the three sweets.
When one thousand have been burned,
light will immediately issue forth from the body of the Buddha in the painted image and encircle the practitioner.
That light then entered the crown of Avalokiteśvara’s head.
The flames of the lamps in the maṇḍala blazed up and increased in intensity.
From the midst of the sky, the sounds of various musical instruments were heard.
The earth shall then tremble and the four directions become clearly manifest.
The practitioner should know that this is the accomplishment (*siddhi*) of the mantra;
at this very moment, one should seek the three kinds of vows.
These are known as the Vidyādharas,
such as Niṣkala-samādhi, Karkaroṭaka, and Malliñjaya.
If one attains the aspiration of a vidyādhara,
one becomes a *cakra-vartī* among the vidyādharas,
with a body that is white in complexion and hair that is deep blue-black.
He immediately assumes the form of an eight-year-old boy;
in the blink of an eye, he can travel hundreds of thousands of yojanas and return to his original place, living for five hundred thousand years.
At the end of life, one will be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
If one attains the vow of signlessness,
one shall become foremost among all those who abide in the great samādhi of signlessness.
When his mind intends to go anywhere,
he can travel a thousand yojanas swiftly and then return to his usual abode.
If the third vow is fulfilled,
one will possess majestic power and sovereignty with a lifespan of five thousand years;
furthermore, one desires to accomplish the Lotus [Sādhana].
Carve a lotus flower from red sandalwood measuring six finger-widths in length and breadth;
during a solar or lunar eclipse,
place it upon seven layers of white lotus flowers.
Place [the image] before the statue and perform the recitation according to the ritual until the three signs appear; thus,
one attains the sign of "warmth."
He becomes King Khagarāja,
possessing strength equal to a thousand elephants and a lifespan of one hundred thousand years;
this is the sign of smoke.
Having attained the samādhi of signlessness,
he becomes a *prajāpati* among all things signless.
Regarding the sixfold division of another's wealth:
One may use one part at will without incurring the offense of theft.
[The lifespan is] one thousand years.
This is the *jvālā* (flame) sign.
He immediately realized the meaning of emptiness and became the Vidyādhara Prajña.
His body was like that of a sixteen-year-old youth, his hair was deep blue-black,
and his strength was equal to that of six thousand elephants.
The radiance and majestic virtue of their bodies will be like those of a hundred thousand suns;
their lifespan shall be one thousand kalpas,
and at the end of life, they will be reborn in the world of Ultimate Bliss.
Such as these: the ritual water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*), the sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), the prayer beads (*akṣamālā*),
the ascetic’s staff (*khakkhara*), flower garlands, the wheel, sword, club,
*musala*, the chisel, battle-axe, hatchet, spear, ox-gallstone, and the garment.
Yellow orpiment, leather sandals, mudrās, vajras,
uṣṇīṣas, alms bowls, saṃghāṭī robes, and the *votuka*— all these,
like the accomplishment of the lotus, yield the three kinds of *siddhi*.
Chapter Three: The Chapter on Accomplishing the Wish-Fulfilling Gem. To accomplish the wish-fulfilling gem, recite the heart mantra five hundred thousand times.
This constitutes the preliminary accomplishment.
Thereafter, take a crystal gem and perform the ritual for accomplishing the lotus as previously described.
During a lunar or solar eclipse, place [the object] upon a single lotus flower and recite the mantra until flames appear.
Thereafter, whatever one seeks in the mind will be fully realized.
Furthermore, one should smear a lotus with the three sweets and protect it for ten nights while raining gold. Moreover,
if one wishes to accomplish the auspicious vase (bhadraghaṭa), [one should proceed as follows].
Accomplish it according to the method described previously.
Furthermore, if one wishes to gain the respectful devotion of yakṣas,
one should smear *sumana* flowers with the three sweets.
The manifestation of the body of the Protector of One Hundred Thousand is *siddhi*.
Furthermore, regarding all those who are ill:
whether they see or touch this practitioner, [they shall be healed].
All shall be healed and cured.
Furthermore, if one wishes to eliminate headaches,
one should visualize oneself as the Buddha.
One rubs their head with the hand;
as one suffers from an ailment, one rubs it oneself.
This same principle applies even to painful sensations in the eyes, ears, heart, ribs, and so forth.
Furthermore, there is another ailment:
if one takes medicine after empowering it seven times with mantras, it will be cured immediately.
Also, when an infant is afflicted by malevolent spirits, [the same method applies].
If one consecrates *kuṇāpī* flowers twenty-one times and scatters them,
one will find peace in one's place of rest. Furthermore, this applies even to those suffering from leprosy.
Take *kirimāla* wood ten finger-widths long,
cut off both ends, and soak them in the three sweets for seven days.
Then take these ashes and mix them with water.
If one smears his body [with this] everywhere, he will be healed immediately.
Alternatively, by reciting it ten thousand times over seven days while burning ten thousand pieces of wood, one may also undergo rigorous training.
Furthermore, there is the *Vajranāgasiddhivārṣika-ratna*.
Anoint agarwood with the three sweets and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times;
he will immediately come to become your brother and daily deliver five hundred taels of gold, which the Master says should be cut from a piece of wood four finger-widths thick.
Furthermore, before my image, recite the mantra once for each offering of a white lotus flower;
when one hundred thousand flowers have been offered, all illnesses will be eliminated.
Moreover, if you wish [to subdue] the yakṣa Sṭidri:
As previously described, one should cut white sandalwood sticks four finger-widths long,
up to a total of one hundred thousand.
Then, seven of these will come to surround the practitioner and speak as follows:
I wish to know what you intend to do.
If you wish to provide food for a thousand people daily on behalf of your son,
or if you desire the deity Sthiravatsakaraṇa.
Anoint one hundred thousand [incantations] with guggulu incense mixed with the three sweets to protect [the practitioner].
Then, the son will come and serve them,
daily providing celestial food and celestial garments.
Furthermore, by smearing a lotus with the three sweets and reciting the mantra three hundred thousand times,
all hidden treasures will manifest.
Having obtained them, one should bestow them upon all sentient beings.
Chapter Four: Healing All Diseases. First, before the image, perform one hundred thousand recitations (*lakṣa*).
Then, take lotus flowers, smear them with the three sweets, and consecrate them ten thousand times.
Next, recite the mantra over white mustard seeds mixed with the three sweets one hundred thousand times.
All illnesses, even those caused by deterministic karma, will be eliminated.
Furthermore, for those possessed by malevolent spirits:
Fill four vases with scented water and empower each one ten thousand times.
Pour them over the crown of the head and bathe; thus, [the affliction] will be immediately removed.
Furthermore, for illnesses such as cold-fever, heat-fever, or those occurring every day, every two days, up to every four days,
one should chant the mantra ten thousand times over salt mixed with the three sweets.
Then, take this ash and empower it seven times.
If one dots the patient’s forehead, they will be healed immediately.
One should act in this same manner for all diseases.
Furthermore, if there are those possessed by ghosts and spirits, even including *piśācas* and *ḍākinīs*, [the same applies].
If one recites this mentally while looking back, [the affliction] is immediately removed.
Furthermore, having empowered the right index finger one hundred and eight times,
one should wave it over the person possessed by a ghost or demon.
He then explained the objects of focus,
stating that he could cause the mind to perform whatever he desired.
Furthermore, he wished to inquire about the events of the three periods of time.
Select a young boy or girl,
bathe them according to the ritual rules,
and smear a small altar.
He anoints his entire body with white sandalwood and camphor incense,
and fashions a garland of mallikā flowers which he fastens upon his head.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.

Then, at a distance of one cubit from the ground, speak of the matter you wish to inquire about. In Guangzhou, there is this flower which is fragrant, white, and sweet; its color is white, its fragrance is sweet, and it may also be substituted by silver coins or *sumana* flowers, etc. This is also permissible.
Furthermore, if one desires to speak of the events of the three periods of time within a dream,
one should smear a lotus with the three sweets and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
Moreover, for those bitten by snakes, or afflicted by various diseases such as spirit-possession and the like, [the same applies].
Whatever afflictions the followers desire to have removed through empowerment shall all be eliminated.
Chapter Five: All Sentient Beings Paying Homage and Recollection. Recite [the mantra] three hundred thousand times before the image.
He performed the preliminary rites;
then, he constructed one hundred thousand stūpas made of fragrant clay,
before which he placed sumanā flowers.
If one recites [the mantra] ten thousand times while consuming the three sweets,
one will immediately attain *siddhi*.
Thereafter, by reciting it at all times, one will obtain abundance.
Furthermore, if one desires to gain the affection of a king,
one should offer *guggulu* incense mixed with the three sweets and recite the mantra ten thousand times;
then the king, along with his entire retinue, will serve him with the devotion of servants.
Furthermore, have an official, as described above, take scented powder,
dip it in the three sweets, and recite [the mantra] ten thousand times. Also,
have all sentient beings of a single village, as described above, do the same.
Mix *guggulu* incense with *śrīveṣṭaka* resin;
by doing so, one will be protected for one hundred thousand recitations (*lakṣa*) at will.
By anointing blue lotuses with the three sweets, one is protected for one hundred thousand [recitations].
He will be revered and beloved by the entire city;
by reciting this mantra over blue lotuses ten thousand times,
all towns and cities shall rejoice.
By anointing the eyes, all that is seen becomes pleasing;
through the hundred-and-eight empowerments, one performs the *āsana*.
By means of the hundred-and-eight empowerments of ox-gallstone (*gorocanā*), one applies it to the forehead.
One will be revered and loved by all whom one encounters.
This is achieved by reciting the mantra twenty-one times while consecrating sweet flag and *agaru* (aquilaria).
One gains victory in debates and disputes;
one's commands and speech are received with faith by all people;
and through the offering of garments, garlands, food, fruit, and so forth.
Whomever he gives [the medicine] to, they all become joyful.
By performing one hundred thousand *āśana* empowerments, all hidden treasures (*nidhi*) are subdued.
When applied to the eyes, one sees monkeys, lions, tigers, wolves, bears, brown bears, weasels, wildcats, snakes, mice, and so forth.
By binding the cord with seven knots and consecrating them, all such terrors will be kept far away.
Chapter Six: The Accomplishment of Purpose. Recite four hundred thousand [times].
First perform the preliminary accomplishment;
then, using white incense and flowers,
offer three sweet substances for one hundred thousand recitations (*lakṣa*).
One will immediately attain siddhi.
By means of agarwood or camphor, one will obtain a thousand coins daily for every recitation of ten thousand (lakṣa).
By protecting [the site] with saffron,
the practitioner shall obtain inexhaustible clothing.
Barley, oil-seeds, mung beans, and rice should be combined.
By reciting the *Rakṣā* ten thousand times, one obtains inexhaustible food.
By reciting the *Aśvaruma* one hundred thousand times,
one obtains the *Aśvagaṇa*.
By reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times with cow’s milk, one obtains a multitude of encounters.
Whatever object one desires, protect it by means of that specific substance;
to seek a son or daughter, protect the rite with sesame oil.
Seek the protection of the great, wise *khaṇḍa* (sweet flag);
the protection of pine wood; and the *śataparṇī* (hundred-leaved) gold.
Each of these three should be performed one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*).
Within the Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes [Sūtra], there are dharmas;
all are accomplished by means of this vidyā-mantra.
Chapter Seven: The Ritual for Accomplishment. Recite before the image.
Fifty thousand recitations constitute the preliminary practice.
With incense of agarwood burning and white lotuses used for protection,
fifty thousand recitations will cause the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa to appear.
The retinue will all come before the practitioner;
as for wealth and treasures, they will all become abundant.
Dip lotus seeds in the three sweets and recite the mantra three hundred thousand times (*tri-lakṣa*).
The auspicious goddess manifests to bring about prosperity and auspiciousness.
By reciting the mantra over three hundred thousand units of pine wood and the three sweets,
all yakṣas will appear and speak these words:
Now, whatever I may desire,
I shall obtain it without fail by following the practitioner’s request.
Take the filaments of the dragon-flower (nāgapuṣpa) and smear them with the three sweets for protection.
Three hundred thousand nāgas came to submit and follow;
with blue lotuses smeared with the three sweets as protection,
three hundred thousand manifested as Vajragarbha.
The vidyādhara, the formless one, and Cakrin—
these three and others may all be sought and attained.
Anoint the lotus with those three sweets for protection.
Before an image of Brahmā, [recite] three hundred thousand times.
The King of Brahmā will appear and grant the aforementioned three vows.
Before an image of Mahākāla, [recite]...
After Sumanas has consumed the three sweets and recited the mantra three hundred thousand times, he manifests as a messenger to accomplish all the rites for Mahākāla.
He wears an elephant hide and carries a spear horizontally; one end of it pierces a human head and the other end pierces a goat. [He stands] before the images of all the deities.
With flowers that are held in high esteem and affection by them,
perform one hundred thousand recitations (*lakṣa*);
they will all come to serve as messengers.
Chapter Eight: The General Attainment. At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I shall now explain the profound and subtle ritual procedures and rules for the various families of these vidyārājas."
The practitioner should first give rise to great compassion for all sentient beings;
be filial toward parents and elders;
and take pity upon those in the realms of suffering.
They possess pure faith in the Triple Gem,
delight in making offerings to all Buddhas,
and remain far removed from such acts as drinking alcohol, negligence, sexual misconduct, killing, and false speech.
Having accomplished this mantra,
one should proceed as follows:
first, on the fifth day of the waxing moon, empower the five purities one hundred and eight times.

Drink it. For each drinking, one obtains purification for half a month. Take small portions of the five pure substances—cow dung and urine—and mix them with ghee, milk, and curd. Place these in either a silver or copper vessel. Perform the consecration (*adhitiṣṭhati*) on the fifth day of the waxing moon, which is the fifth day of the moon's increase.
The mantra for empowering the five purities is:
*Tadyathā oṃ jyotiḥ svāhā*. The heart-mantra for the homage to Tārā is as follows: [one should take] one hundred and eight lotus seeds under an auspicious constellation.
Sit facing east within the meditation chamber.
Recite the empowerment mantra seven times for each lotus seed and pierce it.
The empowerment mantra is as follows:
Oṃ amṛtāṅgāmini śrīmaṇi svāhā. Having thus offered homage and performed the empowerment with the five purities, [the ritual continues].
Whenever one engages in recitation,
one should always first hold the rosary with both hands and empower it seven times with the following mantra: [Mantra]
Oṃ sumatiśrīye svāhā. Having finished the recitation, empower it in this manner and then install it.
The recitation chamber should be entirely plastered with red earth.
Whenever the practitioner voids excrement or urine,
they should recollect the mantra for purifying the defiled body, which says:
Oṃ vajrakurudha mahāmālahana hana paca matha vighnān vidhvaṃsaya jarjara rumudra kuru kurudha hūṃ phaṭ. This mantra provides protection against defilements.
When the ablutions are completed,
one immediately dons the armor with the Armor Mantra (*kavaca-mantra*).
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vidhu vidhu vighāte vidhu prajvalini svāhā. Furthermore, [use] the mantra of Kuṇḍalī.
The mantra for purifying all internal and external obstacles is as follows:
*Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | namaḥ śrīvajrapāṇaye | mahāyakṣasenāpate* ||
Bhadrāye. Namo vajra-krodhānitya-prajvalita-krodha-yugānta-ṭakka-tāpā-vā.
Āḥ asurasarapraśoṣa-hasta āḥ oṃ amṛtakuṇḍali kha kha kha khe khe khidiṣṭha bandha bandha hana hana daha daha paca paca garja garja.

The mantra of the Lotus Family is as follows:
Oṃ namo sarvatathāgatebhyaḥ padmanamovākyāya svāhā. Having performed the *jñānāñjali* (the gesture of wisdom palms joined).
The *mudrā* for the water-vessel rosary is as follows: the mantra is as above;

according to the rules, one should call out "Pra-se-ka-ra" twice, form the *dhyāna-muṣṭi*, and extend the thumb straight up—this is the *mudrā* of Avalokiteśvara’s staff. Form the *dhyāna-muṣṭi* and extend the thumb like a flame.
This is the *kalaśa-mudrā* (vase seal) of Avalokiteśvara: form the *antarmuṣṭi* (inner fist), extend the two thumbs, and slightly bend their upper joints.
This is the *Hayagrīva-mudrā*. The mantras for these three seals above are as previously explained.
The inner binding winds are extended and joined;
the two thumbs are likewise held upright side by side.
This is the second heart-seal (hṛdaya-mudrā).
The second mind is unchanging;
the wind-sign is fixed like a ring.
The mantra for the mudrā of Avalokiteśvara in his white-robed form is as follows:
Oṃ kaci vikaci kaṭaṅkaci svāhā. This is the seal of the Thousand-Eyed One, Nīvaraṇaviṣkambhin.
World-Honored One, seals such as these accomplish all aims and benefits.
I have also already explained this among other dharmas, and it can likewise accomplish the Dharma-gate of the Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes.
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, how does a practitioner accomplish the mantra-dharmas?"
In order to eliminate all obstacles and to provide protection for the root mantra (mūlavidyā),
one should draw a square maṇḍala upon the wall of the practice chamber.
The person who performs the drawing shall observe the eight precepts of the fast.
One should prepare the various colors without using animal glue.
Within this, one should paint a hundred-petaled lotus flower in full bloom.
Complete with the pericarp of the womb, one should inscribe this mantra within the position of the womb. The mantra is:
Oṃ padmanamo nābhavaye svāhā. To the right of the flower, draw a rosary.
On the left is the water vessel (*śītakumbha*). Above the flower, draw a divine cord;
below it, draw a staff.
Make offerings of incense and flowers.
Before this maṇḍala, bind all the mudrās.
By performing such rites as these, [the purpose is accomplished].
All ritual activities and all mudrās shall be accomplished.
World-Honored One, I have spoken this dharma of great power and great valor;
if one wishes to explain the sūtra in its entirety, [it should be done thus].
It cannot be exhausted even in immeasurable kalpas.
This Dharma was previously proclaimed by the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha.
It is the mantra of my own clan, the mantra of the Vajra clan.
All attain siddhi by relying upon this dharma.
This includes all the mantras of the worldly deities, such as Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, Kumāra, the hosts of goddesses, the garuḍas, and the various spirits.
One shall also attain siddhi by relying on this dharma;
by merely reciting it in relation to this, one enters all maṇḍalas.
All sentient beings should pay respectful homage and mindfulness [to this].
All five sins of immediate retribution shall be completely extinguished. At the time of their passing away, [they shall attain liberation].
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara will immediately appear before them and preach the Dharma for them.
After their lives end, they will be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven and shall not fall into the three evil realms.
There may be sentient beings who do not believe in the Three Jewels and are full of stinginess; yet,
upon briefly hearing this sutra, or even reading and reciting it.
They too shall achieve accomplishment before long;
how much more so those who possess pure faith in the Triple Gem.
At that time, the Tathāgata praised the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:

"Excellent, excellent, Great Sattva! You who abide in the state of the Great Sattva with great compassion, you now speak this King of Great Mantras for the sake of the benefit and happiness of sentient beings with pure faith.
After the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara had spoken this sutra, [he sat in silence].
All the great bodhisattvas and arhats, as well as the devas,
nāgas, yakṣas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others, were all greatly rejoiced,
and they faithfully accepted and practiced it.
